newsitem.title: USA: Cash crude prices rise slightly in U.S. Gulf.
newsitem.headline: Cash crude prices rise slightly in U.S. Gulf.

text.p: Cash crude prices edged higher Tuesday, but failed to alter established price ranges for benchmark U.S. outrights and grades.

September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing stood around five cents higher at $20.75-85 a barrel late in the session. September/October spreads, or rolls, were roughly eight cents in favor of the second month contract.

Outright prices found no momentum in either direction. Word that U.N. overseers and Iraqi State Oil and Marketing Organization (SOMO) officials haggled over Baghdad's pricing formula came too late for market reaction, but all indications pointed to easy ratification of the price plan once some details are smoothed out in the coming hours.
For the grades, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James sold at 22 cents over September WTI/Cushing, down from talk in the morning closer to 25-27 cents over.

Traders said West Texas Sour/Midland had moved to a $1.38-40 discount late, from around -$1.35/30 on Monday. Traders said expectations for Iraqi crude liftings in the coming weeks have hampered differentials.
Cano Limon loadings continued to find delays after rebel bombings in Colombia shut Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline operations.
Other talk was muted, save for some WTI/Cushing Postings Plus deals in the mid-$1.90's, traders said.
